title: Groupoid localization of a simplicial shape
statement:
Let $q:K\to S$ be a map of small simplicial sets, using the terminology of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Suppose $S$ is a Kan complex and $q$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. For every quasicategory $\mathscr C$ in a universe containing $K,S$, restriction along $q$ induces an equivalence of enhanced categories
$$q^*:\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathscr C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(K,\mathscr C).$$
The right-hand side is the full subcategory on functors inverting all edges of $K$; its transformations are arbitrary coherent natural transformations, including noninvertible ones. In particular the assertion gives equivalences on their entire mapping spaces, not merely a bijection of equivalence classes of objects or an equivalence of ordinary homotopy categories. Restriction has its usual coherent compatibility with composition of maps of shapes and with postcomposition by enhanced functors.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathscr C)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(K,\mathscr C)$. Both are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the latter being a full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)$. Every edge $f:x\to y$ of $S$ has a two-sided inverse with the required witnesses: fill $\Lambda^2_0$ with edges $01=f$ and $02=\operatorname{id}_x$ to obtain $g:y\to x$ and the triangle for $gf=\operatorname{id}_x$. On vertices $(x,y,x,y)$, take this triangle as face $d_3$, the degenerate triangle $(\operatorname{id}_x,f,f)$ as $d_1$, and the degenerate triangle $(f,\operatorname{id}_y,f)$ as $d_2$. These faces agree on their shared edges and form $\Lambda^3_0$; its Kan filler supplies face $d_0=(g,f,\operatorname{id}_y)$, the other inverse witness. A simplicial map preserves these equations and hence equivalences. Thus restriction along $q$ has image in $\mathcal B$ and defines the stated functor $R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$. We keep all simplices of this full subcategory; no condition is imposed on its transformation edges.

proof.text:
For any small simplicial set $L$ and quasicategory $\mathcal D$, there is an equality of simplicial subsets
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(L,\mathcal D)^{\simeq}=\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal D^{\simeq}).$$
Indeed an $n$-simplex on the left is a map $H:L\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal D$ which sends horizontal edges at every parameter vertex to equivalences, and sends each parameter edge to a pointwise equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. A mixed edge $(a,b)$ is the composite of $(a,\operatorname{id})$ and $(\operatorname{id},b)$, as witnessed by the corresponding $2$-simplex in the product. Its image is consequently invertible as well (the inverse of a composite is the reverse composite of the two inverses). Thus every edge maps to an equivalence, which is exactly factorization through the core. Conversely such a factorization makes horizontal edges invertible and makes each parameter transformation a pointwise equivalence, hence an equivalence by the cited node. An equivalence edge in the ambient functor category between objects of the full subcategory is also an equivalence in that subcategory: its inverse has the same endpoints, and both inverse-witness triangles have only those vertices, so fullness includes all three simplices. When $L=S$, all diagrams already invert its edges by step 1, giving $\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathcal D)^{\simeq}=\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathcal D^{\simeq})$.

source.place: Kerodon 4.4.3.23 (01DA), mixed-edge argument, with the all-edges-inverted condition replacing the Kan assumption on L.

proof.text:
Let $T$ be any small simplicial set in a sufficiently large fixed universe and set $\mathcal D_T=\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathscr C)$, a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Simplicial currying and permutation of the product factors identify
$$\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathcal D_T),\qquad \operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal B)=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(K,\mathcal D_T).$$
For the second identity, an $n$-simplex on either side is the same map $K\times T\times\Delta^n\to\mathscr C$ subject to the same condition: for every edge $a$ of $K$ and vertices $t$ of $T$ and $i$ of $\Delta^n$, its restriction to $(a,t,i)$ is an equivalence. On the right this is precisely the pointwise criterion for the image of $a$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathscr C)$ to be an equivalence. For a monotone map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, both descriptions restrict the same map by $\operatorname{id}_K\times\operatorname{id}_T\times\Delta(\alpha)$; hence the identifications commute with every simplicial operator. Precomposition by $q$ changes only the $K$ or $S$ coordinate, so they also commute with $R$. Taking cores and using step 2 therefore identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(T,R)^{\simeq}$ with restriction along $q$ from $\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathcal D_T^{\simeq})$ to $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D_T^{\simeq})$.

source.place: Kerodon 6.3.1.13 (01MS), proof of (4) implies (2), with its currying identification written explicitly.

proof.text:
The core $\mathcal D_T^{\simeq}$ is Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Apply [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] to $u=q$ and $Z=\mathcal D_T^{\simeq}$. Its hypotheses hold because $q$ is a weak homotopy equivalence in exactly the geometric-realization sense used by that node. With step 3 this proves, for every $T$, a bijection
$$\pi_0\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal A)^{\simeq}\xrightarrow{\ \pi_0(R\circ-)\ }\pi_0\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal B)^{\simeq}.$$
This is a statement for every parameter shape, not just $T=\Delta^0$.

source.place: Core comparison in Kerodon 6.3.1.21 (01MY), using 3.1.7.17 (03PJ) and the realization comparison 3.6.4.3 (03X7).

proof.text: Enlarge the universe once so that $T=\mathcal A$ and $T=\mathcal B$ are allowed; the construction of step 3 and the lemma of step 4 apply in that universe as well. Surjectivity in step 4 for $T=\mathcal B$ gives a functor $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ and a coherent natural equivalence $RG\simeq\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B}$. Here a path of vertices in the core can be made into one equivalence edge by reversing and composing edges using Kan $2$-horn fillings; thus equality in $\pi_0$ gives exactly such an equivalence. Precompose this equivalence with $R$ to get $RGR\simeq R$. Injectivity in step 4 for $T=\mathcal A$ gives $GR\simeq\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$. These two equivalences exhibit $G$ as a quasi-inverse to $R$ in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Explicit two-test-object inverse argument for the criterion used in Kerodon 6.3.1.13 (01MS).

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the functor equivalence $R$ of step 5 induces equivalences on all mapping spaces. The mapping spaces on the right are those of the full subcategory $\mathcal B$, whose definition retains arbitrary coherent transformations between its objects. In particular this conclusion includes noninvertible transformations: only the edges within each $K$-diagram were required to be equivalences.

source.place: Opening compactification choice: full enhanced, rather than ordinary homotopy-category, independence.

proof.text: Finally restriction and postcomposition are the simplicial maps given by composition. For composable maps of shapes $r:L\to K$ and $q:K\to S$, the identity $(q\circ r)^*=r^*q^*$ holds on every simplex; identity maps induce identity restrictions. For an enhanced functor $U:\mathscr C\to\mathscr E$, one likewise has $U_*q^*=q^*U_*$ on every simplex. These maps restrict to the full edge-inverting subcategories since $U$ preserves inverse equations. All iterated identities are equalities of maps on the products with $\Delta^n$, so they supply the usual coherent compatibility at every dimension. The equivalences established above are these restriction maps themselves; no functorial choice of their inverses is needed.
